messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Latency SLO breach detected (p95/p99) for streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Severity: P2. Auto-escalate to oncall-sre. Metrics: p99 CPU/GPU queuing spike, streaming stall events.
oncall-sre: seeing the alert, joining. any service keys?
mike_kaplan: I'm on it. Quick check: which nodes show elevated nvml memory errors?
infra-bot: Metric summary link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/3055550000 — spike started at ~3055550000, p99 went from 120ms -> 3.2s, streaming stall count +420 in 10m.
eng-runtime: initial guess: KV cache pressure + a couple of flaky GPUs hitting thermal throttle/ECC correctables. If nodes degrade, routing should have spilled to dedicated fallback pool but looks like spillover not kicking in.
oncall-sre: running quick query: `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep gpu` to identify pods on suspected hosts.
mike_kaplan: log tail from node gpux-13: ```[nvml] ECC correctable errors rising: 47 -> 312 in 8m
[thermal] GPU temp spike: 84C -> 92C, throttle engaged
[runtime] kV-cache miss ratio spike, streaming stall detected at token 1024
```
sara_li: @mike_kaplan can you cordon gpux-13 and migrate active allocations? we should avoid hitting more ECC corrections.
mike_kaplan: cordoning gpux-13 now: `kubectl cordon node/gpux-13`
mike_kaplan: draining long-running streaming pods: `kubectl drain node/gpux-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` — starting evict.
eng-runtime: while drain runs, apply routing fallback to quantized-64 models and enable prefix-KV bypass on streaming route to reduce token work. Patch posted: `PATCH /routing/policy/streaming {"fallback":"quant-64","max_latency_ms":500}`
oncall-sre: applied routing patch. Watch p95/p99.
infra-bot: Evac status: 18 pods scheduled, 12 successfully rescheduled, 6 pending due to packing constraints. Two of the pending are heavy-realtime streaming connectors (session pins). Might need manual reroute or warm up other nodes.
eng-runtime: temp mitigation: 1) enable spillover to us-west-2-burst pool, 2) lower batch size for streaming to 4, 3) enable KV prefix cache hot-path for affected model versions. Doing (1)-(3) now.
mike_kaplan: started nvml diagnostics: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.used,correctable_errors.volatile --format=csv -l 2` — seeing corrective error bursts correlated with throttle.
eng-runtime: recommend quarantining gpux-13 for maintenance and marking it as 'do-not-schedule' in autoscaler. Also schedule a node-restart after drain if hardware errors persist.
oncall-sre: customer-impact quick check: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE latency > 2000 AND region='us-west-2' SINCE 10m` -> 362 requests affected. Top impacted customers: AcmeCorp (10% of affected), PlayGrid (8%), internal QA (6%).
ce_support: opening ticket CS-9876 for AcmeCorp and PlayGrid with ETA and safety note. Message template: "We've observed elevated tail latency for streaming requests in us-west-2 since <time>. We're actively mitigating and will follow up with timeline."
mike_kaplan: found kernel logs on gpux-13: `Correctable ECC error on 0000:3b:00.0` repeated with thermal throttle events. Suspect flaky DIMM or GPU degradation.
eng-runtime: rolling out canary change to route heavy sessions to fallback pool: `route.override.streams=us-west-2-burst` on 5% -> 25% scale for 10 min, monitor p99.
oncall-sre: p99 after routing change: dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s in 4m. streaming stalls reduced by ~78%. Still higher than baseline, but customer impact significantly reduced.
sara_li: taking over oncall in 10m; @mike_kaplan leave node cordoned and mark incident notes. I'll drive post-mortem and follow up with HW replacement if ECC persists.
mike_kaplan: node cordoned and cordon tag `investigate-ecc-thermal`. w/ logs archived at: s3://infra-logs/incidents/3055550000/gpux-13.tar.gz
eng-runtime: follow-up tasks: 1) keep fallback routing for next 2 hours, 2) run model-quality smoke tests to ensure quant-64 outputs acceptable for affected routes, 3) schedule replacement for gpux-13 if ECC > threshold after reboot.
oncall-sre: Status update to #customer-ops posted. Notifying sales for customers with active sessions > 5.
ce_support: CS tickets CS-9876, CS-9877 created and linked to incident.
infra-bot: Node health post-drain: gpux-13 remains in CORDONED state. After a controlled reboot it still reports correctable ECCs on boot.
mike_kaplan: escalated to vendor hardware team, case HW-44321 opened. Meanwhile, cordoned and quarantined.
sara_li: taking over oncall now. Summary for handoff: mitigation applied (routing fallback + batch reduction + KV hot-path), node gpux-13 quarantined for HW follow-up, p99 reduced to ~1200ms (still above SLO). I will keep monitoring and coordinate replacement.
eng-runtime: note: add automatic fallback trigger in routing policy if node-level ECC > 100/10m in future to avoid manual intervention. I'll draft RFC.
oncall-sre: final note: incident status -> degraded resolved-> mitigated. We'll keep incident open for postmortem. Next update 30m or sooner if regressions. :spiral_calendar: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATE: mitigated at 3055551200 — tail latency improved; node quarantined; customers notified. Incident remains open for postmortem until 3055554800.
